issues.legal_issue: The operative terms of a reconveyance contract are determined by the agreement established by the evidence and read according to its own contents.
material_facts: The plaintiffs relied on an alleged agreement made on the date of the sale and a later writing said to supplement it.
The court found that the alleged earlier agreement was not executed and that the later writing did not refer to it or state that it supplemented it.
The later writing independently set out the terms on which the property could be reconveyed, including a reconveyance price of Rs.25,000.
issues.conclusion: The earlier alleged agreement was not established, and the later writing was an independent agreement governing reconveyance.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the documents and evidence to determine whether the alleged earlier agreement was established and whether the later writing depended on it; it relied on no cited statutory provision or earlier case for this determination.

predicates.reconveyance_contract_dispute: The proceeding concerns enforcement of an agreement to reconvey property.
predicates.earlier_agreement_not_proved: The party seeking enforcement relied on an alleged earlier agreement, but the court found that its execution was not established.
predicates.later_writing_independently_sets_reconve: A later writing sets out reconveyance terms without referring to or depending on the alleged earlier agreement.

issues.definition: When a reconveyance dispute involves an unproved earlier agreement and a later writing that independently sets the terms, the later writing governs reconveyance.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance requires the claimant to plead and prove continuous readiness and willingness to perform the operative contract according to its true construction.
material_facts: The operative reconveyance agreement required payment of Rs.25,000.
The plaintiffs' pleadings and evidence maintained that they were ready and willing to purchase the property for Rs.10,000, and they did not plead or prove readiness and willingness to pay Rs.25,000.
The plaintiffs had paid Rs.5,000 in two instalments, but the record contained no specific statement that they were ready and willing to pay the full reconveyance price.
The plaintiffs sought specific performance of the reconveyance agreement.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs failed to establish readiness and willingness to perform the operative contract, so specific performance was unavailable and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, and Explanation (ii) require an averment and proof of readiness and willingness to perform the contract according to its true construction, assessed from the pleadings and evidence as a whole and maintained from institution of the suit through decree. The court relied on Syed Dastagir v. T.R. Gopalakrishna Setty, AIR 1999 SC 3029, for reading pleadings as a whole; Motilal Jain v. Ramdasi Devi, (2000) 6 SCC 420, for assessing whether the plaint as a whole indicates readiness and willingness; and Umabai v. Nilkanth Dhondiba Chavan, (2005) 6 SCC 243, for assessing conduct in light of all attending circumstances and the evidence. The court noted the discretion under Section 20 but did not decide whether its exercise would otherwise have been equitable.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brings a suit seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.operative_contract_requires_full_perform: The contract found to govern the dispute requires the claimant to perform specified essential terms.
predicates.claimant_pleads_or_proves_readiness_only: The claimant's pleadings or evidence show readiness to perform less than the essential performance required by the operative contract.

issues.definition: In a specific performance suit, when the operative contract requires performance that the claimant does not plead or prove readiness to provide, specific performance is denied for failure to establish readiness and willingness.
